- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or volatile (alternating ±0.5–1.0), model often underestimates or overshoots; apply mean reversion to mid-range of recent 5–7 day average.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > 75% of recent 10-day high), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 10% below peak or adjust downward by 3–5% for next 3 periods.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 15–20% in next 2–3 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive; apply 1–3% downward bias to first 5 forecasts.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.33) over 5+ days, model tends to underestimate; add 1–2% upward bias to forecast for next 3–5 periods.
- If model forecast exceeds true outcome by > 3% for 3 consecutive days, apply downward correction of 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
